A new sponsor from the utility company assesses the capital improvement projects and decides to reorganize it into a program. They invite seven companies to discuss their approach to monitor and control the program and its constituent projects. Where should the program manager incorporate this input? A. Program management plan B. Vendor management matrix C. Component project charters D. Program risk management plan

A biometrics firm has a facial recognition program with multiple components and project managers. The project manager from the mobile device division escalates a vendor-related risk to the program manager. After assessing the risk, the program manager determines that this risk may impact other projects within the program. However, this risk has a low degree of impact and probability of occurring. What should the program manager do first? A. Obtain a risk reserve from the executive sponsor, and execute a contingency plan. B. Communicate the risk to all project managers to manage at the component level. C. Add the risk details and analysis to the program risk register. D. Brainstorm with the project manager to develop an appropriate risk response.

A program manager is developing a program management plan by integrating the plans of constituent projects. During this effort, the program manager learns that a resource is critical to more than one component and there is a time overlap for their availability. When creating the program resource management plan, what should the program manager do first? A. Ask the human resource (HR) manager to hire an additional resource. B. Analyze resource capacity and capability with component project managers. C. Develop the program schedule in accordance with resource availability. D. Revise the plan to ensure the allocation of all needed resources.

A global communications company’s cloud-based platform will host its video network using both on- and offshore teams. The program management office (PMO) assigns a program manager with little experience executing global initiatives. What should the program manager do to resolve competing resource needs within components that could impact the entire program’s overall delivery date? A. Improve communications between component project managers so they can work together to perform resource leveling. B. Require project managers to perform resource leveling in their schedules to automatically take into account availability and dependencies for key resources. C. Optimize integration of the component projects by working with the project managers to align resource skill sets and availability to the program. D. Revisit assignments on a weekly basis to manually level resources, thereby limiting burnout and preventing underutilization.

A manufacturing company is redesigning various component projects that comprise a large customer-facing program. One of the component projects is payment of back-end rebates. There is disagreement between the marketing and sales teams on how much should be rebated. What should the program manager suggest be used as standard measurement criteria for the success of all constituent projects to meet stakeholder expectations? A. Cost-benefit analysis, return on investment (ROI), and payback period B. Actual cost (AC), planned value (PV), and earned value (EV) C. Stakeholder engagement plan, risk management plan, and communications management plan D. Needs analysis, feasibility study, and integrated benefits management plan

A program manager assigns a project to a qualified project manager. The client rejects the project manager due to a lack of proper qualifications to manage such a project. What should the program manager do first to resolve this issue? A. Apply competence assessment techniques. B. Assign a different project manager to this project. C. Reassess the project manager's qualifications. D. Schedule a review meeting with the client.

A municipal agency manages a city's water and wastewater infrastructure. A regulation requires the replacement of sewer lines throughout the city at a cost of US$2 billion over 30 years. The city has been managing this program with various program teams and has a project controls office in place to track projects separate from the program management team. A program manager is hired to standardize all deliverables from component projects under the program. What should the program manager do next? A. Create a program performance analysis report. B. Establish a program management office (PMO). C. Develop a stakeholder register. D. Develop a program management framework.

The program sponsor requests that a junior project manager take over a complex component project as a professional development opportunity. The component project currently has several senior subject matter experts (SMEs) working on it and also has dependencies with other large projects to deliver key benefits to the organization. The junior project manager is both excited and concerned about the assignment and decides the best next step is to: A. Request a meeting with the project sponsor to discuss the project and ensure they are qualified. B. Accept the assignment as a challenge and an opportunity to acquire new skills and seek advice from a senior project manager. C. Begin work on the project immediately to determine the important skill gaps and then request professional training. D. Meet with the project team to share that they cannot accept the assignment because there is too much risk.

An IT-related program has a critical team in a region experiencing a crisis. Due to uncertainty about the region’s changing environment, the company’s senior leadership asks the program manager to decrease dependencies on the critical team. What should the program manager do first to mitigate the impacts of this request? A. Revisit the program management plan to clearly identify how decreasing critical team dependencies will impact component projects. B. Meet with the steering committee to request assistance and influence in obtaining additional resources. C. Update the procurement management plan and begin the request for proposal (RFP) process to replace the critical team by staff augmentation. D. Level resources and empower the critical team to complete its work before regional instability impacts its efforts.

A new performance financial system is delivered to all business entities on time following a 1-year implementation program. After 6 months of utilization, the global finance department, one of the main beneficiaries of the program, determines that the quality and level of granularity of the financial data is not sufficient for them to analyze the key performance indicators (KPIs) defined. Additionally, the global finance department is missing the analytical tools required to understand the causes of unsuitability. To address these shortcomings, the global finance department submits a request for a follow-up initiative through the process defined by which of the following documents? A. Benefits sustainment plan B. Benefits management plan C. Benefits register D. Benefits transition plan

Company A has been acquired by company B. All the programs and initiatives under company A now follow company B's organizational strategic goals. What should a program manager do to ensure that the program meets the organization's strategic goals? A. Manage the program delivery phase. B. Analyze the benefits management plan. C. Engage the program steering committee. D. Assess the program benefits schedule.

A nonprofit organization launched a program to reduce its dependence on regularly decreasing government funding sources. This program’s goal was to pay 50% of its operating expenses by selling its services to the for-profit sector. After 3 years, the goal was reached, deemed complete, and transitioned to operations. Eighteen months later, the organization discovers that its dependence on government funds has now increased to 80%, even though its operating budget has largely stayed the same. What should the program manager have done to avoid the issue of program benefits being unrealized after more than 1 year of implementation? A. Had the operations manager follow the benefits management plan B. Utilized schedule compression techniques to deliver value sooner C. Worked with the operations department after the program was transitioned D. Developed program transition and benefits sustainment plans as part of the transition to operations

A multinational organization is centralizing its IT infrastructure, which is spread across 16 countries. The organization will embark on a transformation journey that encompasses three main areas: 1. Assessing which technology/tooling should be retained for the target data center. 2. Establishing a common set of processes supporting the new way of delivering services. 3. Revising human resources (HR) processes to account for the new improved services for employees in the various countries. The assigned program manager is preparing the business case for the program. Which document should be present in the program manager’s business case? A. A detailed plan showing dependencies among the constituent projects B. A comprehensive analysis of the different compensation packages offered in the 16 countries C. An inventory detailing all physical and logical components in place and the employees in scope D. A cost-benefit analysis of the different scenarios, presenting their respective contributions

During the steering committee meeting, the program manager shares the customer tests results. When should a program manager approve the closure of a component project? A. When acceptance criteria of the project are met B. When the project has delivered the project benefits C. When program deliverables are complete D. When project deliverables are complete

A program completes all component projects and all identified benefits are being delivered. However, the program sponsor is concerned that long-term benefits may not meet organizational performance parameters. What can the program manager do to address the program sponsor's concern? A. Send the benefits management plan to the program sponsor for review. B. Review the benefits sustainment plan with the component managers. C. Set up a meeting with the sponsor to review the benefits transition plan. D. Review the benefits register and check for the benefits requested.

A program manager is leading a program introducing a new customer relationship management solution. As the program progresses, the sponsor and other stakeholders are satisfied with the pace of the program's performance. A stakeholder from the sales department now requests a new feature to integrate the platform with another application. The program manager advises that this is out of scope and requests additional funding via the formal change management process, and the new scope is approved. What should the program manager do next? A. Secure additional approvals from senior stakeholders. B. Assign a new project manager to own the delivery of the new project. C. Redefine the priorities of the existing program components. D. Cancel an existing component and reallocate resources to the new project.

A program manager is assigned to a large cross-functional program that includes five different technologies and multiple workstreams. Some potential stakeholders have conflicting program expectations. What should the program manager do next? A. Send out satisfaction surveys and document the results in the program's stakeholder engagement plan. B. Update the stakeholder register to document stakeholders’ positions relative to the program. C. Document stakeholder expectations in the program’s risk register to determine their influence. D. Share the approved program business case with key stakeholders and conduct interviews with them.

A program is in the closing phase and is preparing to start delivering benefits to stakeholders. The stakeholders did not receive adequate information to sustain the program once in operations and are concerned the program will fail once the program team exits. What should the program sponsor do? A. Direct the operations manager to allocate a resource to the program to ensure that knowledge transfer and process development occur before closure. B. Direct the program manager to review the necessary plans to ensure benefits can be transitioned and sustained after program closure. C. Direct the program manager to assess the impact of this change and follow the established change management process. D. Direct the operations manager to allocate the necessary resources to establish proper plans for accepting the benefits and processes after program closure.

A program has several components and operations activities embedded within its scope. At the beginning of the definition phase, a program manager needs to consider risk throughout the program along with the interdependencies with the operational activities. Knowing the impact can be much larger than the program itself, what should the program manager do to ensure that operations is included in the program risk management activities? A. Create a program risk management strategy that includes operations B. Conduct a program risk assessment to determine where help is needed C. Ensure that a program performance report is sent to operations stakeholders D. Develop a program risk response strategy to address operational concerns

A financial company is transitioning to a new billing system and is approaching completion. Before the transition starts, a mandatory requirement must be met to check on some program performance metrics. To address this requirement, a phase-gate review has been scheduled for the following month. In preparation for this important review, what can the program manager do to ensure the program is on track to meet the requirements? A. Schedule a health check to review key performance indicators (KPIs) B. Schedule a health check to review the program governance plan C. Schedule a health check to review the benefits management plan D. Schedule a health check to review benefits realization and issue logs

A program manager is initiating a cross-industry program comprised of several projects. Due to multiple constraints and the complex nature of different industrial requirements, the investors hold a conservative attitude regarding the program risks. What should the program manager do when developing the program risk strategy? A. Encourage the stakeholders to be optimistic and set higher thresholds due to sufficient reserve funding B. Set lower risk thresholds based on the stakeholders' risk preference and organizational risk appetite after risk assessment C. Establish the risk thresholds based on the differences among the stakeholders' preferences recorded in the program risk response strategy D. Identify each risk based on the risk thresholds grounded into a number of criteria set in the program risk response strategy

A program manager for a multiyear software development program following an agile approach has identified several program risks and assigned them to the appropriate component teams for mitigation. The program manager notices that some of the teams are not following the risk management plan and are not reporting the status of their risk responses. What should the program manager do next? A. Change the risk management plan to allow more flexibility and autonomy for the component teams. B. Conduct a program risk audit and review the risk register to ensure alignment and accountability C. Escalate the issue to the program sponsor and request that the risk management plan be enforced D. Accept the issue as long as the program deliverables are not affected by the risks

During the delivery phase of a program, a program manager found opportunities to improve benefits by initiating multiple components within the current program structure. What should the program manager do next? A. Present the new opportunities to the program governance board for approval to initiate B. Assess the new and current components per the current program prioritization C. List the program's components by teams as they are needed to maximize benefits D. Determine the required resource allocation and interdependencies to initiate the components

A program manager is kicking off a new program in a company. The program team is comprised of team members with less than 1 year of experience. What can the program manager do to help prevent lack of experience from impacting benefits delivery? A. Ask senior team members to mentor the junior team members B. Record the risk in the program risk register and begin work on high-risk projects C. Ask the program sponsor to extend the delivery schedule to reduce risk D. Engage with the team members to provide coaching and training

A program has had a history of difficulties reaching agreements on scope priorities among its agile component projects. What should the program manager do proactively to help resolve this unproductive pattern? A. Work with Scrum leads to facilitate better decisions B. Play the role of mediator for program scope C. Negotiate with product owners and agile teams to align with objectives D. Engage stakeholders to develop a stakeholder engagement matrix.

A program is in the formulation phase. A program manager needs to document major program milestones that highlight the realized benefits for the stakeholder community. Which document should the program manager reference to create this artifact? A. Program integrated master schedule B. Roll up of component project schedules C. Benefits management plan and register D. Program schedule management plan

A program manager is starting a new program and developing a strategy to ensure stakeholders are informed of ongoing program activities over the life cycle. What is a key component of this strategy? A. Frequency and depth of program information B. Collection and distribution of program information C. Engagement needs of the program stakeholders D. Influence and interest of program stakeholders

The program components have been completed, and the program manager needs to capture and validate benefits delivery. What should the program manager do next? A. Modify the program master schedule B. Consult the benefit management plan C. Update the program roadmap D. Review and update the benefit register

A program manager is leading a software development program. The program sponsor asked the program manager to accelerate delivery so the company can realize revenue sooner. What should the program manager do? A. Review the components and prioritize key features that are aligned with strategic objectives B. Explain that the current software release plan is aligned with the needs of the intended users C. Share the schedule and explain the compression risk is above established thresholds D. Identify the key components and prioritize features that require the least amount of effort

A program client reports quality issues with components that have been delivered and requests changes to address those concerns. How should the program manager address the complaints? A. Start the program escalation process because the customer complained B. Follow the program change procedure to implement changes the customer has requested C. Review the program governance plan for the next steps to address this concern D. Determine where the quality variance originated to best address the concern

A program has a number of risks that directly impact program benefits. The governance associated with risk management needs to be strong to ensure program benefits are realized. Which two artifacts should the program manager review and reinforce to enable strong, effective risk management and governance to deliver program benefits? (Choose two.) A. Risk register and issue log B. Program change control C. Tolerance and threshold levels D. An escalation matrix E. Program charter

The program manager determines that some component project managers are not effectively managing their projects due to communication issues. What should the program manager do? A. Establish a transparent program environment B. Instruct the project managers to address the concerns C. Share the issue with the program sponsor D. Update the project's key performance indicators (KPI)

A program manager has taken over a program in progress for several years. During a program governance review, the new program manager realizes that several projects do not have key performance indicators (KPIs). What should the program manager do? A. Develop a benefits management plan B. Align the benefits with the strategic objectives C. Ensure that the projects are delivering value D. Develop a key performance indicator dashboard

A program sponsor and a program manager are working together to determine which components to include in a program to deliver the maximum benefits and value to an organization. The interdependencies among the components need to be fully understood. What action should the program sponsor and program manager take regarding component selection? A. Align the components' efforts to the organizational strategy and the components' business cases B. Monitor benefits realization to ensure they remain strategically aligned to the organization's goals C. Optimize the components' path to achieving the benefits and providing value to the organization D. Define the outputs and outcomes of the components that will contribute to the delivery of benefits

A program manager for a sustainability program that aims to reduce carbon emissions and waste generation has implemented a program-level continuous improvement process that involves engaging stakeholders, benchmarking performance, and implementing best practices. The program manager encountered some resistance and challenges from some of the key stakeholders who were reluctant to change their behaviors and processes. What should the program manager do next to address these challenges? A. Negotiate incentives or penalties with the stakeholders to motivate change B. Provide coaching and training to the stakeholders to facilitate change C. Reassess the stakeholder analysis and communications plan to address their concerns D. Escalate the issue to the program sponsor and request intervention

A program consists of four projects and three of those projects are executed by an outsourcing company as it requires specialized skills that are only available with the outsourcing company. The program is considered high risk as the organization has never implemented such a program before. During the initial executive steering committee meeting, one of the key influential stakeholders has concerns regarding the risk management process for this program. What should the program manager do to alleviate the stakeholder’s concerns? A. Ask the project managers to set up weekly sessions with the stakeholder to review project risks B. Schedule a meeting with all stakeholders to understand their risk concerns more in depth C. Provide weekly progress updates to the stakeholder that include insights into the risk register D. Share the program risk register with the stakeholder and explain how it is monitored

A new program manager has been assigned to an existing program. While reviewing the benefits initially mapped to the program components, the program manager finds that some quality key performance indicators (KPIs) are not meeting the measurements. Some critical deliverables are due in a few weeks, and the program and benefits will be impacted if no action is taken. In which phase of the program is the program manager currently? A. Benefits analysis and planning B. Program definition phase C. Benefits delivery D. Program audit

An experienced program manager is leading an international program and is mandated to enforce published industrial standards. Several professional key stakeholders are reluctant to accept the program manager's authority. These individuals seek to usurp the program manager's authority by convincing the program sponsor to agree that their permission and approval for all program work are required. What should the program manager do first? A. Meet with the program sponsor and stakeholders to clarify the importance of aligning with the industrial standards B. Compromise for the good of the program due to the stakeholders' level of influence C. Acquire the program sponsor’s support and reinforcement of the mandate for following the industrial standards D. Demonstrate the benefit of the program's alignment by sharing the industrial standards with all stakeholders

A program manager is leading an overseas bullet train program across multiple countries. The program has been successful for a long time owing to the program team's technical expertise and rigorous planning. However, one country's terrain is complex and its mountains are steep which will increase the risk for the whole program. What should the program manager advise the program sponsor to do? A. Ask the program team to delegate more decision-making in this situation B. Require the program team to monitor progress and success more diligently C. Respond to foreseen risks and activate the program contingency reserves D. Include a higher frequency of health checks in the program governance plan

A program sponsor is concerned that a program investment may not realize the promised benefits. What should the program manager do to show the program sponsor that the program is delivering the defined benefits? A. Review the benefits realization plan with the program sponsor B. Document progress in the benefits register and share it with the program sponsor C. Evaluate the opportunities and threats affecting benefits D. Confirm that the program benefits are aligned with the strategic objectives

The organization has authorized a merger and acquisition (M&A) program. During the planning phase, the program manager scheduled an online M&A training course for the 5 project managers. After the planning exercise is completed, one of the project managers informs the program manager that the training course is not needed because the project manager will apply project management best practices from many years of industry experience. How should the program manager handle the situation? A. Escalate to the request to Human Resources (HR) B. Approve an exception for the project manager to skip training C. Request the project manager assist with the training session D. Require all project managers to take the training

A program manager has been directed to validate selected projects for alignment with organizational strategy. How should the program manager proceed? A. Create and update the program mandate B. Revise and validate the program charter C. Update each component business case D. Review alignment with the organizational strategic plan

A program manager of a large infrastructure program that follows a predictive approach has prepared a program status report for senior management and other key stakeholders. The report contains information on the program scope, schedule, cost, quality, risks issues, and benefits. How should the program manager present this report to the stakeholders? A. Send the report to all stakeholders via email and ask them to respond with any questions or comments B. Schedule a meeting with all stakeholders and present the report using slides and charts C. Publish the report on the program website and notify the stakeholders via email D. Customize reports for each stakeholder group and communicate using the appropriate method

An organizational leader in a company has initiated a new service offering after reviewing the latest marketing report that revealed a strategic opportunity for the company. A new program is approved with several projects aligned under this program. How should the program manager assess the health of the program? A. Schedule within the program governance plan B. Communicate through the program benefits plan C. Review health metrics during a program steering committee meeting D. Provide dashboard communication to stakeholders

A program sponsor instructs a program manager to quantify and document measurable outcomes for the stakeholder community to avoid future risks related to unclear benefits delivery. What should the program manager do for the program sponsor? A. Ask the program sponsor to share objectives B. Update the program governance plan C. Create key performance indicators (KPIs) D. Brainstorm objectives with the stakeholders

A new program component depends on an external provider that has shown a lack of commitment in the past. The component is on the critical path and the program manager wants to avoid as many risks as possible. What should the program manager do? A. Use the provider but move the component off the critical path to avoid risks B. Cancel the component to eliminate all the potential risks by avoiding dependency of the provider C. Ask the customer to be in charge of managing the relationship with the provider D. Establish frequent reviews with the provider to monitor potential risks

The portfolio manager believes there is an opportunity to create a new product offering creates a new program to bring the capability to market. The business case was approved by the sponsor. What should the program manager do next? A. Develop the program charter B. Update the program roadmap C. Create the benefits plan D. Establish the strategic plan

A program manager for an extensive healthcare program that aims to improve patient safety and satisfaction has developed a benefits realization plan that outlines the expected benefits and their owners, metrics, and timelines. How should the program manager communicate this plan to the stakeholders? A. Send the stakeholders a copy of the plan and request feedback B. Create a video for the stakeholders that showcases the plan and its benefits C. Present to the stakeholders a summary of the plan and highlight the key points D. Invite the stakeholders to a workshop to explain the plan and address their concerns

The component project managers reported their projects are behind schedule These project managers are blaming their team members. What should the program manager do first? A. Update the key performance indicators (KPI's) to reflect the delays B. Promote a productive and cooperative team environment C. Hold a separate meeting with the project managers D. Adjust the project schedules using available slack

A complex technology program consisting of nine projects is at risk of delayed deliverables. A team member found a valid alternative solution that allows parallel implementation of three components previously planned to be implemented sequentially. Which document should the program manager update? A. Program roadmap B. Program business case C. Program work breakdown structure (WBS) D. Program issue log

An organization is starting a program that includes several component projects. Many of the stakeholders require different types of information, and communication is vital to the program's success. Where should the program manager record all information? A. Stakeholder register B. Communications register C. Stakeholder engagement plan D. Program communications management plan

An organizational leader in a company has initiated a new service offering after reviewing the latest marketing report that revealed a strategic opportunity for the company. A new program is approved with several projects aligned under this program. What should the program manager do to validate the benefits delivery of the overall program? A. Maintain through the dashboard B. Update through the benefits plan C. Initiate through the business case D. Review through governance

An education reform program will be following an adaptive approach for its execution. A feasibility study on the expected outcomes was conducted and several viable options were identified. The next step is to identify the program's critical performance measures. Which document should the program manager use to identify and maintain the program's key performance indicators (KPIs)? A. Benefits management plan B. Business case C. Benefits register D. Program governance plan

A program manager has experience in a transnational finance and bank program. During the program formulation phase, the program manager asks all relevant parties to identify their expectations for this program's outcome and their interest in staying informed and involved during delivery. Which document will help the program manager? A. Program communications management plan B. Program communications assessment C. Program charter D. Stakeholder engagement plan

A program manager is leading a complex program involving multiple stakeholders with conflicting interests and expectations. The program manager has conducted a stakeholder analysis and developed a stakeholder engagement plan. What should the program manager do next to demonstrate leadership and ownership? A. Communicate the program vision and objectives to all stakeholders and solicit their feedback B. Implement the stakeholder engagement plan and monitor the stakeholder satisfaction levels. C. Escalate any issues or risks that may affect the stakeholder relationships to the program sponsor D. Negotiate with the stakeholders to align their interests and expectations with the program benefits

Component projects in a program produce items that are integrated and delivered to stakeholders incrementally. Some of these items are not working correctly, causing the stakeholders to become concerned. What should the program manager do to address this situation? A. Ensure all items conform to the quality standards of the program B. Provide a refund to the stakeholders who received the defective items C. Escalate the issue to the steering committee for a policy review D. Ask the project managers to conduct quality inspections of future items

A leading healthcare company is implementing an electronic medical records system across its healthcare facilities and is in the program delivery phase. Several updates on the deliverables have been made since the last program status update. The executive sponsor, primary business stakeholder, and key functional manager from the healthcare facility have requested an interim update. What should the program manager do next? A. Produce an updated status report for all stakeholders and distribute it ahead of the normal schedule B. Utilize the process defined in the program communications management plan to communicate these updates C. Provide these stakeholders with updates since the last program status update via email D. Update the online program dashboard with the changes that have occurred since it was first published

Many stakeholders have recently left a program to retire or be assigned to other programs. The program manager wants to update the replacement stakeholders on the program goals. What should the program manager provide to the new stakeholders? A. Program business case B. Program charter C. Program master schedule D. Program roadmap

Organizational environment could lead to products and services becoming stale over time, which could directly impact the organization's competitive advantage. One risk could have diverse impacts across organizational programs. How should the program manager address this risk? A. Learn through people, processes, technology, and information B. Emphasize quality is brought in as an element C. Hire vendors through the procurement process D. Learn from competitors and their strategies

A program manager has already signed an endorsement by the large and complex IT application program. During the execution of the program's course, several component managers raise different issues to the program manager by the program escalation process, then the program manager reviews these issues with the component managers and figures out these issues should stay at the component level. What is the cause of these issues? A. Program risk attitudes are set too optimistic B. Program risk thresholds are set too narrow C. Program risk tolerances are set too high D. Program risk appetites are set too aggressive

A program manager has performed quantitative risk analyses for all identified program risks while creating a program risk management plan. The program manager and their team have also defined risk responses for each risk. What should the program manager do next to ensure effective program risk management? A. Review and update the risk register B. Monitor and control risks C. Communicate risks to stakeholders D. Implement risk responses

A program manager is preparing a program team to work virtually due to a health crisis. The program team has never worked virtually in the past for an extended period of time. What should the program manager do? A. Speak to program team members and focus on program objectives and how to achieve deliverables B. Defer to the executive management for guidance and direction in this situation C. Update the risk register and monitor as part of the program risk monitoring and controlling activity D. Identify as a risk, work on a program communication plan and update the replacement

The intermediate benefits of an international e-commerce program decrease incrementally and chronologically during the delivery phase. These decreases are due to currency inflation and increased transportation costs. Which documents should the program manager use to document these changes? A. Benefits management plan and benefits register B. Benefits management plan and program governance plan C. Benefits management plan and program roadmap D. Benefits management plan and issue register

During a global health crisis, the senior leadership of a hospital system asked a program manager to evaluate a crucial clinical program due to uncertain patient needs and poor project component quality. What should the program manager do first? A. Cancel the existing components to ensure program benefits are achieved B. Evaluate and update the program change management plan C. Put the existing components on hold and perform a quality assessment D. Evaluate and update the project change management plan

A program is actively delivering incremental benefits. Several approved change orders are affecting the schedules of multiple component projects in the program. The program sponsor is unclear on when specific benefits are being delivered because of all the schedule changes. What should the program manager do to prepare for a meeting with the program sponsor? A. Create a change order requesting funds necessary to meet the schedule B. Ask the project managers to update the component schedules C. Aggregate the component schedules into a detailed master schedule D. Update the program roadmap based on the component schedules

Two new component projects need to be incorporated into a program due to some changes in the organization's priorities. These changes are generating a new demand for resources not previously considered. Getting the resources to be fully productive could take a long time. What should the program manager do first? A. Reject the new projects due to insufficient resources to address the arising needs B. Outsource the two new projects to external companies so the program schedule is not impacted C. Ask the human resources (HR) manager to start the recruiting process to get all the resources the program needs D. Look within the organization for resources with the required or similar level of skills and assign them to the new projects

A project manager for a component, calls a program manager for advice. The project manager plans to schedule technical training for the project team on the critical skills needed for project delivery and asks the program manager which document to update. Which document should the program manager advise the project manager to update for the required training? A. Stakeholder engagement plan B. Training management plan C. Risk management plan D. Resource management plan

A company's senior leadership asked a program sponsor to make some changes to the benefits a program delivers each month. The senior leader and program sponsor are both concerned this request could create a schedule slip but are willing to accept the changes if the program team can continue to deliver each month. What should the program manager do to address this situation? A. Assess the roadmap to determine if updates are necessary B. Notify the component project managers of the changes C. Record this risk in the program risk register with a score D. Present a change order to the program sponsor with the adjustments

A program manager decides to schedule a program meeting with all team members to ensure all program team members understand the need to maximize productivity. What specific point should the program manager emphasize? A. Build ownership within the team and act as an enabler of the program B. Understand the specific roles and responsibilities of the program team members C. Focus on handling program escalations and risk mitigation D. Centralize ownership to prevent individuals from making decisions on the program

A program is unable to use an office building for at least 6 months. The program sponsor provided office space in a distant location. The program sponsor has asked the program manager to provide an update on the effects of this unplanned change. What should the program manager do first? A. Require team members to work at the distant location until the local site is available B. Investigate the option for team members to work remotely until the local site is available C. Evaluate the impact of the location change to the program cost schedule, and risk D. Notify the program sponsor that work will cease until the local site is available

A program manager with experience is taking over a large sewage treatment program that involves the interests of all parties. During program formulation, the enterprise trades off from the benefit-cost perspective: the environmental protection government considers the health of local inhabitants. Which technique will help the program manager to set clear engagement goals? A. Stakeholder onion diagram B. Power/interest grid with stakeholders C. Stakeholder engagement objectives D. Principles of stakeholder engagement

Multiple component projects in a program are behind schedule, creating a risk that the program will not deliver the benefits contractually required the following month. This will cause the company to default and damage its brand reputation. What should the program manager do first? A. Implement the actions prescribed in the risk register B. Notify the steering committee and program sponsor C. Contact the legal council assigned to the program D. Increase funding for the projects that are at risk

Benefits achieved in the current stage of a program are being assessed against the program's progress. The customer feels the program is being delayed. Which artifact should the program manager use to address the customer's concern? A. Program schedule B. Program benefits register C. Program business case D. Program roadmap

A program manager will need to document the benefits sustainment plan after completion of a program. Which two actions should the program manager include in the plan? (Choose two.) A. Include the business owner in the benefits realization process B. Align the expected benefits with the organization’s goals and objectives C. Monitor the benefits delivered by the program components. D. Identify and assess the value and impact of the program benefits E. Assign responsibility and accountability for benefits realization

During initiation of a program component, a program manager asks a component manager to design the component's key performance indicators (KPIs) in compliance with the overall program KPIs. During which phase is this activity occurring? A. Program planning phase B. Component transition phase C. Program delivery phase D. Component oversight phase

A governance body appoints a program manager to a technology innovation program. During the program delivery phase, several key stakeholders ask to be updated about whether intermediate benefits have been realized as planned. What should the program manager do? A. Hold the closure phase meeting to review the benefits management plan B. Hold the phase gate meeting to review the benefits management plan C. Hold the decision points meeting to review the benefits management plan D. Hold the health check meeting to review the benefits management plan

A program manager has been assigned to lead a newly chartered program. The program sponsor is asking for a roadmap and a risk assessment. The program manager has scheduled a risk workshop with program stakeholders and component leaders to assess the risks. What does the program manager need to do to complete the program roadmap? A. Review the organizational goals B. Examine the program business case for inputs C. Determine the program governance plan. D. Establish a business strategy

A program stakeholder is questioning the benefits and performance of a program. Which documents should the program manager share with this stakeholder to demonstrate the program value delivered? A. Program benefits register, program benefits management plan and program governance plan B. Program benefits management plan, program governance plan, and program performance reports C. Program business case, program benefits register, and program performance reports D. Program integrated schedule, program business case, and program scope management plan

A leading high-technology enterprise is initiating a new adaptive program. During the delivery phase, one component falls behind the expected schedule because another component is sharing resources. Which documents should the program manager update? A. Program roadmap and program schedule management plan B. Program roadmap and program master schedule C. Program roadmap and schedule model principles D. Program roadmap and program risk register

A program manager for a construction program composed of five components is working on the first monthly status report based on preestablished key performance indicators (KPIs). The program sponsor asks the program manager about the contents of the report, which will be sent to program stakeholders. How should the program manager respond? A. The program report includes the program schedule and the schedules of all five components B. The program report includes a summary of the program's progress at the program level C. The program report includes a progress summary of the program and all its components. D. The program report includes a progress summary of the five components and the program risks

A company very new to program management is working on a pilot program. The program manager of this pilot program will encounter many improvement opportunities throughout the program life cycle. How should the program manager address the need for continuous improvement throughout this pilot program? A. Initiate a second pilot program to utilize the lessons learned from this pilot program B. Ensure that the updated processes are implemented in the proposed program management office (PMO). C. Review and update the program management plan regularly with process- related updates D. Review and update the program governance plan regularly with process- related updates

A risk management strategy should be defined to help discover opportunities and threats to a program and realization of its benefits. What should the program manager do to simplify the ongoing discovery of opportunities and threats as a part of their risk management strategy? A. Complete an initial risk assessment to analyze threats and opportunities to the program B. Create an environment for communicating and addressing program risks and uncertainties C. Update the benefits management plan and program roadmap with the new risks and uncertainties D. Update the benefits register for new opportunities and threats affecting benefits

During delivery of an overseas construction program, the planned budget is overspent due to unforeseen inflation and the currency exchange rate. What should the program manager do to mitigate this issue? A. Update the program budget B. Use the management reserve C. Use the contingency reserve D. Update the cost baseline

In a transformational program, all projects are on track and delivering their objectives. However, stakeholders are hesitant to take on the new processes, because performance in the current environment may not be representative of actual performance. Stakeholders fear the program will fail to provide the service required. To assure positive performance in the current environment, what should the program manager do? A. Ask the program steering committee to endorse the new processes, current program schedule, and deliverables B. Discuss concerns with stakeholders and mitigate them by changing the processes that will be delivered C. Request feedback from all relevant project managers to ensure the new processes will perform better than the current processes D. Meet with stakeholders to ensure they understand that the expectations for the new processes are superior to the current processes

A program sponsor requires the governance board to meet each month and that each member receive a weekly status report. The program's customer holds a contract requiring the program manager to host a weekly status briefing. How should the program manager ensure all stakeholders receive the information they require to ensure successful program execution? A. Create a comprehensive stakeholder register B. Reference the information distribution plan C. Develop a capabilities compliance matrix D. Update the strategic communications plan

A large infrastructure program has three component projects. Project 1 is being built in collaboration with a vendor company and has a high-level risk that could delay the timeline and increase the costs of two of the three projects. Project 1 could also delay the program delivery date. Fortunately, the program team reviewed the program management plan and realizes there are contingency reserves at the program and project levels. What should the program manager do to utilize the contingency reserves? A. Ask the two project managers of the impacted projects to use their contingency reserves because the high-risk delay will impact them B. Ask the project manager of project 1 to use its contingency reserve because of the high risk on this project C. Use the program contingency reserves because the high-level risk impacts the whole program and two of its components D. Review the contract with the procurement office to understand if the contingency reserves can be used to prevent delays

During a program progress review, a key stakeholder disagrees with the program's engineering team, which is responsible for the program's delivery schedule. This leads to a conflict in which both parties try to impose their expectations for the program schedule. What should the program manager do? A. Facilitate a negotiation session among stakeholders to address their conflict on expectations B. Facilitate a negotiation session among engineering team members to address their conflict on expectations C. Ask the program sponsor to explain the program’s expectations D. Ask the engineering team to revise the program schedule

A procurement lead raises an issue that will impact the delivery date of a key component from the primary vendor. This delay will impact the timeline of three of the projects in the program. How should the program manager address this situation? A. Assess the program impact and work with the vendor to provide a resolution to the issue B. Communicate with and ask the project managers to report on the significance C. Conduct a meeting with the project managers to resolve the issue D. Assess the program impact and provide recommendations to the steering committee

An organizational leader has been reviewing the newest marketing strategy plan and believes there is an opportunity to begin a new service line. A new program is approved with several active projects realigned under this program. What should the program manager do next? A. Establish the program roadmap B. Develop the program charter C. Establish the program committee D. Develop the program definition

A program sponsor of a large financial organization informs a mergers & acquisitions (M&A) program manager that the current M&A program, still in the planning phase, may be impacted due to the recent acquisition of another company. The program manager decides to review and update the program risk management plan and risk register. Which type of risks should the program manager focus on? A. Program risk thresholds B. Program risk response strategy C. External program risks with vendors D. Strategic alignment risks of the program

A program manager asks a project team to accelerate the timelines of multiple deliverables to avoid a regulatory compliance issue for the organization. The team completes the accelerated request. What should the program manager do next? A. Ask the project manager to thank the teams and purchase a small gift card for each team member B. Invite leadership to the next team meeting and publicly thank team members for their leadership C. Inform leadership during the stakeholder meeting that the accelerated timeline was met D. Send an acknowledgment email to the team for their hard work to meet the accelerated timeline

A program steering committee has initiated an 8-year overseas infrastructure construction program. This program will compliment several other overseas programs already underway. The three key engineers have already been assigned to other programs and are unavailable to commit to the new program. What should the program manager do? A. Recruit several senior technical experts and retain those who can adapt to the program style B. Report this gap to the program sponsor and work together to seek a win-win solution C. Estimate the gap between expected competence and actual competence, then provide training and recruitment for the program D. Ask the program sponsor to recall the three core technical experts from the other programs regardless of their busy schedules

Several program managers in an organization are looking for opportunities to establish continuous improvement. What should the program managers recommend to senior leadership? A. Establish a portfolio structure and align all programs into it B. Incorporate continuous improvement metrics into the benefits register C. Add continuous improvement measurements in each program D. Set up a program management office (PMO) in the organization

A program manager is using a hybrid approach in a healthcare improvement program. The program manager has defined and validated the program benefits management plan with the benefits owners. What should the program manager do next to establish the program's key performance indicators (KPIs)? A. Establish the benefits governance structure and assign roles and responsibilities B. Establish the benefits measurement criteria and methods for each benefit C. Establish the benefits realization baseline and track it throughout the program life cycle D. Establish the benefits transition plan and ensure alignment with operational processes

What would prevent a program manager from completing program closure once a program has been completed? A. Incomplete realization of all program benefits B. Failure to update the benefits register C. Not obtaining program steering committee approval D. Not updating the financial management plan

A governing program sponsor will select a program manager during program formulation. What should the program manager do to ensure the program objectives are aligned with the business strategy? A. Review the program strategy B. Develop a program roadmap C. Rewrite the program charter D. Create a program business case

A program manager is working on an approved complex healthcare program composed of five components. The program manager is in the definition phase and has started capturing key performance indicators (KPIs) to ensure the overall benefits generated will be delivered by the target organization. The core objective of this program is to transform the way medical records are accessed by patients and caregivers in the digital era. What should the program manager do next? A. Integrate the program components B. Develop the business case C. Develop the program roadmap D. Prepare the benefits register

A program team starts working on a new program. These team members have never worked with one another in the past and this could result in high risk and low quality. What should the program manager do to ensure program success? A. Allow dissent among team members to motivate a diverse culture. B. Create a trusting environment for differences of opinion to emerge. C. Ensure conflicting messages are sent by team members on a regular basis. D. Enforce a collective-central decision to trigger conflict resolution.

An organization wants to know if upgrading all the legacy applications deployed in a specific group of customers will prompt them to buy additional services. This upgrade will increase profitability. A program manager has been appointed to a program initiated to address this need. How should the program manager begin this effort? A. Update the program risk management register B. Engage with the sponsor to approve program charter C. Create a program business case D. Develop a detailed program roadmap

Two component project managers are competing for limited resources which has led to conflict between the project managers and caused program delays. What should the program manager do? A. Allocate the resource to any of the project managers B. Allow the project managers to develop a resource plan C. Resolve the conflict at the program level D. Implement program conflict management

An ongoing research program has many external dependencies and is subject to mandatory requirements from regulatory bodies. The program requires filing several documents with government and regulatory bodies for approval. Failure to comply with regulations poses a significant risk to success of the program. What program activity should the program manager pay close attention to for regulatory compliance? A. Program quality assurance and controlling B. Program communications management C. Program information management D. Program risk monitoring and controlling

A program has a new sponsor and a few new governing board members. The program manager has been asked to brief the new members on the program's benefits, component mappings, associated target dates, and responsibility matrices. Which document will the program manager be presenting at the review meeting? A. Program management plan B. Benefits management plan C. Benefits register D. Program benefits plan

The program technical lead has uncovered a significant issue that will result in a 3-month schedule delay. The program manager has acknowledged the issue and its impact. Who should the program manager communicate this situation to? A. Component managers B. Program sponsor C. Program stakeholders D. Team leads

A component shipment was delayed due to a global supply chain issue. This resulted in stretching the schedule of one component in a program, yet the program manager was still confident in delivering the program far ahead of schedule at no extra cost. Despite this, the customer wants to apply a delay penalty on the delayed component, because the contract is unclear about considering global issues as a force majeure. After alignment with internal key stakeholders, what should the program manager do next? A. Update the program roadmap and request utilization of the contingency reserve for the penalty. B. Update the program business case and request utilization of the management reserve for the penalty. C. Work with the legal team to manifest an interpretation of the clauses that can support filing a case in court. D. Negotiate with the customer to avoid the penalty in return for crashing the full program schedule.

A program manager is providing a fifteen-minute high-level program update during a monthly organizational town hall meeting. While speaking to the bullet points, many attendees raise their hands to request additional information about the overall program. What should the program manager do? A. Setup an open meeting to provide an in-depth update B. Establish multiple forms of program communications C. Take the additional time to address the questions raised D. Request inclusion on the monthly town hall agenda
